description: Opt in to API-key providers (paid tokens). Absent or false: subscription-only, and no API provider is constructed.
Subscription-mode overrides; every field has a default. See docs/subscription-decisions.md.
Structural tool rules: the only tool denials, held in every permission mode (turns/tool-gate.ts).
Credential references only; do not put tokens in settings.
Kingdom subscription pools this Foundry draws main-thread logins from: one per owner's Signet (URL, credential file, pool selection).
Project-scoped integration grants. Independent of inference resource selection. Restart to apply.
Which Kingdom owner's pool (and spread or selection) a given thread draws its login from, by thread id.
Explicit thread-to-source UUID assignments, applied on Foundry startup.
Background domain review phase; does not override classifier/router or executor profiles.
The feedback lifecycle: capture, tuning prompts and the role-file changes they apply (docs/FEEDBACK-LOOP.md).
The local journal (docs/THREAD-TREE.md spec A).
Days a middleware call's raw rows (its full input) stay in the journal after its turn is reduced; Archive only ever gets the reduced entries. Default 30.
The Warden pre-filter: a local decision model skips a Warden on a confident "not my domain". Off by default (every Warden is asked); `{ "enabled": true }` opts in. See docs/subscription-decisions.md.
How often the Wardens' guard fires: `per-turn` (default), once over a turn's whole tool activity when the turn's tool activity ends; or `per-call`, on each tool call (Aron, 2026-10-15).
The composition view: one ladder (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, auto memory, role files) composes the instructions and domain knowledge of every role; see docs/usage-and-context.md.
Global defaults — executor provider/model + classifier provider/model.
The provider new threads run on (e.g. `claude-code`, `codex`).
The model new threads run on.
Which local login (a native authentication source) threads use by default.
Which Kingdom owner's subscription pool threads use by default.
Reasoning effort for Codex threads; omitted, Codex's own default.
Classifier/router provider. Defaults to same as executor if omitted.
Classifier/router model. Defaults to same as executor if omitted.
Vendors (keyed by vendor id: anthropic, openai, google, ...), each with an on/off switch and its subscription and API modes (models/vendors.ts).
This Foundry's installation name: what Kingdom pairing names it. Default "Foundry on <host>".
This machine's icon where machines are shown (Watchtower actors, Watching): a glyph and a slot of the theme's categorical palette (`--layer-0` to `--layer-11`).
The icon's shape (anvil, bolt, leaf, moon, peak, wave, star, hex).
The icon's colour: a slot of the theme's categorical palette, 0 to 11.
The message box: one box with a destination label (Thread · /btw · /aside), or a box per open view.
Show a message box per open view (Thread, /btw, /aside) instead of one box with a destination label.
Global agent templates (keyed by agent ID). Projects inherit these by id; a project override of the same id wins. A fresh install is seeded from defaultAgents(): one executor.
The agent's id: its key in `agents`, and how projects extend or override it.
What the agent does in a turn (executor, classifier, router…).
FLOW.md role: context-routing, domain-advising, execution, correctness-checking, signal-reconciliation.
Domain this agent operates in (e.g., "docs", "security", "cross-thread").

Human-readable description of this agent's role and responsibilities. File path relative to project root (e.g., ".foundry/agents/security-librarian.md"). Explains: what this agent does, which layers it reads/writes, who it delegates to, why.
System prompt for this agent.
LLM settings — provider/model default to global if omitted.
The model this agent runs on; omitted, the global default model.
Temperature — set per agent. Classifiers/routers want 0, creative agents want higher.
Which layers this agent can READ (empty = all). These are the layers whose content appears in this agent's assembled context.

Which layers this agent can WRITE (empty = none). The Librarian owns thread-state. A Warden owns no configured layer: it writes only its generated thread-knowledge layer, and reads its knowledge from the composition view.
Warden: source ids its domain knowledge composes from, before the composition view's files (docs/usage-and-context.md, "Composition view"). A project extension appends its own.
Tool names that trigger this configured Warden's post-action guard. [] disables guards.
Peer agent IDs for delegation.
Max call-chain depth.
Whether this agent can use tools (true) or is text-only (false). Default: true for executors, false for classifier/router.
Extended thinking / reasoning effort. "none" | "low" | "medium" | "high" | number (budget tokens).
Permission level for code execution runtimes. Default: "bypass".
Execution environment for this agent's tool calls. Default: "bash" (via Claude Code provider). See ExecutionEnv type for options.
Browser-specific config. Only relevant when executionEnv includes browser access.
Browser interaction mode.
Whether to share authenticated browser sessions across agents.
Allowed URL patterns (glob). Empty = allow all.
Blocked URL patterns (glob). Takes precedence over allowedUrls.
Whether to capture screenshots for context.
Max page loads per dispatch (prevent runaway navigation).
Per-call timeout in ms.
Enable prompt caching for this agent.
Whether this agent is active.

When this agent runs in the pipeline: - "always": runs on every request (default for classifier, router) - "on-demand": available but only invoked when middleware/router explicitly requests it - "conditional": runs when its condition matches the current classification/route context
Condition for "conditional" invocation. Ignored for other modes.
Match if classification.category is one of these.
Match if any classification tag overlaps with these.
Match if route.destination is one of these.
Global layer templates (keyed by layer ID). Projects inherit these by id; a project override of the same id wins. A fresh install has none: a thread is unwrapped until one is configured.
The layer's id: its key in `layers`, and how projects and agents refer to it.
Domain knowledge ownership. An enabled domain-advising agent must explicitly own this layer to register a custom expert; passive layers do not spawn actors.

Human-readable description of this layer's job in the system. File path relative to project root (e.g., ".foundry/layers/conventions.md"). Explains: what knowledge domain it covers, when it's relevant, who writes to it, what the warmed content looks like.
What shape the warmed content takes — helps humans and agents understand what's inside. E.g., "JSON array of convention objects", "Markdown documentation index", "Compact thread-state JSON".
Instruction prompt for this layer.

Semantic segment of the layer's CONTENT in the reading view. Optional: a configured layer without it keeps the legacy id-based classification. Only "domain-knowledge" (configured/published cache) or "thread-knowledge" (generated, thread-private) are accepted; the prompt is always an instruction.
Data source IDs that feed this layer.
Staleness threshold in ms (0 = never stale).
Agent IDs that can write to this layer. Undefined = any agent.
Whether this layer definition is enabled.

When instances of this layer are included in context assembly: - "always": included on every request (default for system, conventions) - "on-demand": only included when explicitly requested via route.contextSlice or middleware - "conditional": included when its condition matches classification/route context
Condition for "conditional" activation. Ignored for other modes.

Where the content comes from: a file, database, URL, markdown, inline text, the Archive, or instruction files.

Memory-backed ("file") sources only. Widest visibility this source exposes to a thread: "thread" (default) = the thread's own captures plus project/global publications; "project" = publications only; "global" = globally published knowledge, identical for every project.
Memory-backed sources only. Also expose unowned legacy records written before ownership existed. Off by default: legacy records are preserved on disk but never become shared knowledge implicitly.

`archived`: hidden from the viewer's project list until unarchived; its settings and threads are kept and it still runs. Absent: live, its runtime status (active or idle) derived from its threads.

This project's chorus: the region Wardens its threads run. Merged over the repository's own `<project>/.foundry/project.json` `chorus`, these settings winning. Region Wardens run only when `enabled` is true; absent, the project has no chorus and regions present are reported as off. In a resolved project view this is normalized (`enabled` effective, `layers` absolute); see docs/usage-and-context.md, "Chorus".
Run this project's region Wardens. Off by default.
The one regions directory the chorus reads (absolute or relative to the project; default `.foundry/regions`).
Several regions directories in order, a later layer's region replacing an earlier one (e.g. template base, then this project).
The `consumed` trigger: Wardens are asked when a thread takes in a work item. Off by default.
Ask the Wardens when a thread takes in a work item (a ticket, spec or issue it read). Off by default.
Globs on a tool's name; a matching call's output is the work item. Default `DEFAULT_CONSUMED_TOOLS`.
Globs on a read file's path, relative to the project; the file is the work item. Default `DEFAULT_CONSUMED_PATHS`.
The work item is clipped to this many characters, with a marker. Default 12,000.
The reception charter (`CHORUS_RECEPTION`): how the main thread reads a chime, held once as a standing layer. On with the chorus (itself opt-in); `false` leaves it out, e.g. for a baseline.
How the chorus's Warden regions classify (classify/): their stages, at most three. Omitted, one stage, today's Warden. The machine's list replaces the repository's whole.
Its stages, each `{ model?, effort?, doc?, outcomes?, reason?, task?, pointer?, escalate?, deadline? }`.
How Herald regions would classify: the socket only. Heralds are not built; their regions do not run.
